clue.text: Fine member of parliament to be chicken?

parts.note: F is the standard abbreviation for fine, as on pencil leads
a group of owls is called a parliament, so one member of it is an owl

explanation.surface: A politician fined and branded a coward.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Member of parliament' wants to be an MP; here the parliament is the collective noun for owls. The question mark flags that a chicken is just one example of the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: A chicken is a domestic bird, the commonest example of poultry kept for eggs and meat.

clue.text: Going to pieces without pot? That's not very nice

indicators.note: without tells us to take the cooking vessel away from the longer word

parts.note: someone going to pieces with anxiety is panicky
a pan is a cooking pot

explanation.surface: Someone falling apart for want of cannabis says it's not pleasant.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pot' looks like cannabis but is a kitchen pan.
explanation.definitionFit: Icky is informal for distastefully unpleasant or sickly, so it describes something not very nice.

clue.text: Run unhindered, changing hands

indicators.note: changing hands swaps the right-hand letter for the left-hand one in the word for unhindered

parts.note: unhindered means free

explanation.surface: A runner breaks loose, with the baton passed from one hand to the other.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Changing hands' swaps R (right) for L (left).
explanation.definitionFit: To flee is to run away from danger, so run is a direct synonym.

clue.text: Partly regret spitting over better advisor

indicators.note: over in a down clue says the letters are read upwards, i.e. backwards
partly says the answer is a part of the run of letters in regret spitting

explanation.surface: Someone half-sorry about spitting at an adviser who knows better.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Partly' finds RETSPIT across regret spitting, and 'over' turns it round. 'Better' is one who bets, not 'superior'.
explanation.definitionFit: A tipster gives racing or betting tips, so a person who advises those placing bets.

clue.text: Eye star possibly drinking whisky in the past

indicators.note: drinking means one piece takes the other inside it
possibly signals the letters of eye star could be arranged otherwise

parts.note: rye is a kind of whisky distilled from rye grain

explanation.surface: A starlet with a sparkling eye is downing whisky, as in days gone by.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Possibly' rearranges EYE STAR to YESTEAR, and 'drinking' puts RYE inside.
explanation.definitionFit: Yesteryear means time gone by, so used adverbially it stands for 'in the past'.

clue.text: Drink from cans, hugging cool male, oddly drunk

indicators.note: hugging means the word for cans wraps around the other letters

parts.note: tins are cans

indicators.note: drunk tells us the letters of cool plus the odd ones of male are jumbled
oddly picks the first and third letters of male

explanation.surface: A cocktail poured from tins, with a man who was cool and now oddly drunk.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Drunk' seems to describe the man but signals the anagram, making OMCOLL from cool plus the letters 'oddly' picks from male; the cans are 'hugging' it. A Tom Collins is a long gin drink.
explanation.definitionFit: A Tom Collins is a gin cocktail with lemon, sugar and soda, an example of a drink.

clue.text: Rock singer initially with Mick?

indicators.note: initially means take only the opening letter of singer

parts.note: and means together with
Mick Jagger is a Rolling Stone

explanation.surface: A question about which rock singer goes with Mick.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rock' looks like music but is geology. Mick is Jagger of the Rolling Stones, so a Stone.
explanation.definitionFit: Sandstone is a sedimentary rock made of cemented grains of sand.

clue.text: Fat chanteuse returned cases

indicators.note: returned means the hidden letters are read backwards
cases means the word chanteuse contains the answer's letters

explanation.surface: A plump singer gave back her cases.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cases' finds TEUS inside chanteuse and 'returned' turns it round.
explanation.definitionFit: Suet is the hard fat from around an animal's kidneys, used in cooking.

clue.text: Support for bad member's stolen weapon

parts.note: a sling supports an injured arm
the possessive ending gives S
hot is slang for stolen goods

explanation.surface: An injured arm's sling turns out to be a stolen weapon.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bad member' is an injured limb.
explanation.definitionFit: A slingshot is a catapult, a simple hand-held device for hurling stones, so a weapon.

clue.text: Model man perhaps about to leave non-professional type

indicators.note: to leave tells us the letter for about departs from the longer word

parts.note: clay is a modelling material, so a model man could be a clay person
C is circa, Latin for about
a man is an example of a person

explanation.surface: A male model is about to quit, being no professional.
explanation.walkthrough: C (circa) leaves CLAY PERSON, a figure modelled in clay.
explanation.definitionFit: A layperson has no specialist training, so is an amateur outside any profession.

clue.text: Nothing gained by training writer

indicators.note: gained by means the training letters take the zero inside

parts.note: PE is physical education, training
O looks like zero, nothing

explanation.surface: An author who got nothing out of training.
explanation.walkthrough: PE (physical education) takes in O.
explanation.definitionFit: Edgar Allan Poe was the American author of tales of mystery and horror.

clue.text: Keen on headless horse

indicators.note: headless means the horse's first letter is removed

parts.note: a pinto is a piebald horse

explanation.surface: An enthusiast for a horse that has lost its head.
explanation.walkthrough: A pinto is a piebald horse.
explanation.definitionFit: Being into something informally means being enthusiastic about it, keen on it.

clue.text: Slip into Henley?

definitions.meaning: to ... a garment is to put it on, slip into it
... Henley is the Eagles' drummer and singer

explanation.surface: Changing into something for the Henley regatta.
explanation.walkthrough: Henley evokes the rowing regatta's blazers, but it is the musician's surname.
explanation.definitionFit: Donning clothes means putting them on, and Henley's first name supplies the second sense.

clue.text: Description of poor kippers — or suggestion for overly good ones?

definitions.meaning: kippers are sleepers, and poor sleepers are insomniac
split in two, the word tells heavy sleepers to doze less

explanation.surface: Smoked fish of poor quality, or advice for ones that are too good.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Kippers' is slang for people having a kip (a sleep), not smoked herrings.
explanation.definitionFit: Those who sleep badly are wakeful; read as two words it advises those oversleeping to rest less.

clue.text: Injured life-saver bringing in student will get fine decoration

indicators.note: bringing in means the student letter is taken inside
injured says the letters of life-saver are damaged into a new order

parts.note: L is a learner, a student driver

explanation.surface: A hurt lifeguard, helped by a student, earns an honour.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Injured' rearranges LIFESAVER; 'bringing in' adds L.
explanation.definitionFit: Silver leaf is silver beaten into very thin sheets, used to ornament surfaces delicately.

clue.text: Rich living: German's over for the first time

indicators.note: for means in place of, and the first picks the earlier of the two time letters

parts.note: extant means still existing, living
über is German for over

explanation.surface: A lavish life: the German is over it for the first time.
explanation.walkthrough: In EXTANT the first T is swapped for UBER.
explanation.definitionFit: Exuberant can mean luxuriant or abundant, as with lush rich growth.

clue.text: I bite cop wrongly arresting Republican before anyone stirred?

indicators.note: arresting means the jumbled letters hold another inside them
wrongly says the letters of I bite cop are set in a different order

explanation.surface: A suspect bites a policeman who was wrongly arresting a Republican.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Wrongly' rearranges I BITE COP and 'arresting' takes R inside. The question mark: 'before anyone stirred' means before life began.
explanation.definitionFit: Prebiotic describes conditions on Earth before living organisms emerged, so before any creature moved.

clue.text: Clothe in undergarment the French discarded

indicators.note: discarded means the French article is thrown away from the garment

parts.note: a girdle is a corset-like undergarment
le is French for the

explanation.surface: Getting dressed in underwear the French have thrown away.
explanation.walkthrough: 'The French' is LE, the French article.
explanation.definitionFit: To gird is an old verb for dressing or equipping someone, as in girding with armour.

clue.text: Treated badly with forces leaving, crowd united

indicators.note: leaving says the force letters depart from the two words

parts.note: to crowd a space is to fill it
fused means joined, united
F is the symbol for force, so forces gives two Fs

explanation.surface: Abused when the troops pulled out and the mob came together.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Forces' looks military but is two Fs, one removed from FILL and one from FUSED.
explanation.definitionFit: Ill-used means abused or mistreated, a direct synonym of handled badly.

clue.text: King cut short by top officer taps part of ear

parts.note: CO is commanding officer
taps are marked C and H, cold and hot

indicators.note: cut short means the king's name loses its last letter

parts.note: Lear is Shakespeare's king

explanation.surface: A king curtailed by a senior officer who taps his ear.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Taps' are bathroom ones, C and H. LEAR, Shakespeare's king, cut short.
explanation.definitionFit: The cochlea is the spiral cavity of the inner ear that converts sound into nerve signals.

clue.text: Wave finally at son with a friend in Paris

indicators.note: finally means take the last letter of at

parts.note: un ami is French for a friend

explanation.surface: Waving at last at a son who is with a French friend.
explanation.walkthrough: 'In Paris' means the words are in French: UN AMI.
explanation.definitionFit: A tsunami is a huge sea wave caused by an earthquake or undersea landslide.

clue.text: Kind of dash about on lake

indicators.note: about turns the dash name round so it reads backwards

parts.note: an em dash is a long dash in printing
re means on, concerning

explanation.surface: A hurried rush round on a lake.
explanation.walkthrough: EM is a printer's dash; 'about' reverses it.
explanation.definitionFit: Mere is a poetic or regional word for a lake or pond.

clue.text: Police officer reported description of Blofeld's position?

indicators.note: reported says the phrase is spoken and the answer is what we hear

parts.note: Blofeld heads the villains' organisation SPECTRE in the Bond films, so he is in Spectre

explanation.surface: A police officer reporting where the Bond villain Blofeld stands.
explanation.walkthrough: Blofeld is the head of SPECTRE, the criminal organisation in James Bond stories.
explanation.definitionFit: An inspector is a police rank, above sergeant in Britain.

clue.text: Caught greeting foreign character

parts.note: C is the cricket abbreviation for caught
hi is a greeting

explanation.surface: Caught out saying hello to someone from abroad.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Foreign character' is a letter of a foreign alphabet, not a person.
explanation.definitionFit: Chi is a letter of the Greek alphabet, so a character from a foreign script.

clue.text: City disturbance brought to a premature conclusion

indicators.note: ending early means the last letter of the word for disturbance is cut

parts.note: a riot is a public disturbance

explanation.surface: Unrest in a city cut short.
explanation.definitionFit: Rio de Janeiro, the Brazilian metropolis, is commonly called Rio.

clue.text: Actor fit to make comeback

indicators.note: making a comeback means the word for fit is turned round to read backwards

parts.note: able means fit, capable

explanation.surface: A performer fit enough to make a comeback.
explanation.definitionFit: Idris Elba is a British actor known for Luther and The Wire.

clue.text: Firm flying out in case

indicators.note: flying sends the letters of out in case scattering into a new order

explanation.surface: A business flying out just in case.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Firm' looks like a company but is an adjective.
explanation.definitionFit: Tenacious means holding firmly, persistent and determined.

clue.text: Company provided cap

parts.note: if means provided that

explanation.surface: A firm supplied headwear.
explanation.definitionFit: A coif is a close-fitting cap, once worn by nuns and lawyers.

clue.text: Expel vacant student holding up distance-learning provider

indicators.note: in a down clue the student letters sit below, supporting the provider

parts.note: OU is the Open University, the UK's distance-learning university

indicators.note: vacant empties the word student, leaving only its outer letters

explanation.surface: A clueless student is thrown out of an online university course.
explanation.walkthrough: The Open University (OU) is Britain's main distance-learning university.
explanation.definitionFit: To oust someone is to drive them out, to expel them from a position.

clue.text: Fast ship unloaded on track

indicators.note: unloaded empties the ship of its middle letters, leaving its ends

parts.note: RY is railway, a track

explanation.surface: A speedy ship is unloaded beside the railway.
explanation.definitionFit: Spry means nimble and lively, quick in movement.

clue.text: One at sea and tense after auction finished early

indicators.note: after puts the tense letter following the other piece
finished early means the auction word loses its last letter

parts.note: a sale is an auction
T is the grammatical abbreviation for tense

explanation.surface: A nervous person all at sea after an auction ended early.
explanation.walkthrough: 'One at sea' looks like confusion but is a sailor.
explanation.definitionFit: An old salt is a seasoned sailor, so a salt is someone who goes to sea.

clue.text: Grant for one to conceal order error for canteen

indicators.note: to conceal means the Hollywood name hides the other letters inside it

parts.note: Cary Grant was a film star, so Cary is an example name
OM is the Order of Merit
a miss is an error

explanation.surface: A grant to cover a mistake in an order for a canteen.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Grant' looks like money; it is Cary Grant, the actor.
explanation.definitionFit: A commissary is a store or canteen supplying food, especially on a military base or film set.
